decisions.reason: After surviving its first review year, this core door-handle family likely shows at least acceptable market traction versus aspiration and remains well aligned with the firm's main system offering.

The mitred handle family still fits the firm's design-led architectural niche, and continued market presence suggests management sees enough acceptance to keep learning rather than redeploy resources.
As another adjacent handle line in the certified core portfolio, it would usually be retained unless it now clearly lagged comparable launches, which its continued presence does not indicate.
Its award-backed visibility and role as a coordinated door-and-window collection point to performance comfortably above aspiration, giving management little reason to withdraw it.

The finish remains the most droppable item because variants can be pruned if uptake is thin, but as a low-resource extension that supports the firm's design and one-stop specification logic it is still more likely to be kept.
